paper_metadata.title: Novel strength-electrical conductivity synergy in Cu-based composites reinforced with TiZrNbTa high entropy alloy

evidence.quote: An ultra-high strength TiZrNbTa (TZNT) high-entropy alloy (HEA) with good plasticity was attempted as a new reinforcing phase

high-strength conductive composites. This work utilized a combination of a two-step ball milling method (first HEA mechanical alloying followed by fabrication of TZNT HEA/Cu hybrid powder) and a spark plasma sintering process to prepare the bulk TZNT HEA/Cu metal matrix composites (MMCs).
The designed TZNT HEA alloy with an equal atomic ratio was synthesized by the mechanical alloying (MA) process using Ti, Nb, Ta, ZrH2 (Purity ≥ 99.5%) raw powders.

The TZNT HEA alloyed powders were successfully obtained after a ball milling (BM, QM-3SP2, Nanjing Chishun Technology Development Co. Ltd.) process of 40 h. The applied rotating speed was 350 revolutions per minute (rpm), and the weight ratio of the stainless-steel balls and powders is 15:1.
